q: Ever since I had the baby, it feels like things have been so out of control. I find myself constantly asking if it is just the age or if my parenting is ruining everything.
cx: Mother of a four-month-old and a nearly-three-year-old.

q: I feel like other people (family) are appalled by her behavior and my parenting sometimes. Even the dog is crying during her meltdowns these days.
cx: How family react to the meltdowns.

q: Her dad and I have different approaches to this. He is starting to get frustrated and insist she take bites of new things or finish certain things
cx: Low-pressure meals versus the father's insistence.

q: She speeds up if I set the limit because she knows that I really will step in but this makes me feel like I'm threatening/pressuring her all the time when she just wants to be silly.
cx: Bedtime takes hours; timers work but feel like pressure.

q: Anyway, at this point I feel like I am failing at everything and I can't tell if I am "creating a monster" or if some kids are just high spirited and toddlers are tough. I just want to cry.
cx: Her closing line.

q: Wow that felt judgy lol. I promise you I’m not a lazy parent, I was just trying to look for insight and best approach for him.
cx: Heavily pregnant mother asking about night potty wake-ups; commenters call her lazy.

q: I read the 3 day potty training method book and the author mentioned that, I feel like it makes sense from what she was saying with how it can cause some confusion, but I also see how having a potty available in some other rooms is helpful too. Kids are all just individuals and you have to find what works for them I guess!
cx: On the book's advice to keep the potty in one place.

q: I was fully expecting my son to rely on a night diaper for years lol.
cx: Child, three weeks into training, wakes to pee.

q: I promise my kid is fine and not confused. He’s been doing fine all day. I’m done defending myself y’all are ridiculous lmao
cx: Last reply after more criticism.

q: I've never seen advice on what to do in this situation, only how to deals with no in answer to a question you actually ask of them.
cx: 22-month-old says 'no' to things nobody proposed.

q: I've tried ignoring, reassuring, asking her to stop saying it, but she just keeps on going. It's really stressful listening to her say no to do many things that we don't even need to be doing anyway and watching her get more distressed about it.
cx: Toddler grows more distressed each time.

q: I guess I'm so tired I hadn't considered that! (I have a newborn as well!)
cx: Reply to the idea she means another time.

q: I also bought her a calendar specifically for tracking her progress.
cx: Pregnant mother runs a 20-item daily checklist tied to stars and allowance for a nearly-four-year-old.

q: I'm currently on day 3 of potty trainning and I've read Oh Crap! Potty Training. I align with a lot of info in the book, however I'm really struggling to see my 22 month old son's pee signal.
cx: Day three of the book's method.

q: I had interpreted from the book that there would already be a signal and that I would need to watch for it. I definitely am not anticipating him being trained in three days
cx: Reply about signals developing over time.

q: unfortunately my husband and I both work full-time. I'm on a week vacation from work (the most time I could get off at the moment) to ~start~ his potty training so I'm hoping I will be able to notice some signals to provide to the daycare for when he goes back.
cx: One week off to start training.

q: I have a tendency to go down rabbit holes and I didn't want to go overboard with the potty training info. Researching all the different methods can make things confusing and overwhelming (at least for me).
cx: Why she stuck with one book.

q: I attribute the lack of progress to the daycare because they only take the toddlers to the potty once every two hours, which I think is nowhere near often enough imo.
cx: Six weeks later, little progress after he returned to daycare.

q: I also attribute his lack of progress with potty training due to our work schedules. The amount of awake-time he spends at home during the week is very minimal
cx: Same update.

q: I have just resigned myself that it will take longer for him due to the daycare and our work schedules interfering
cx: Same update.

q: The problem is he’s all of a sudden getting angry with my boyfriend. If me and my boy are playing and he comes and joins, he gets so mad and hits.
cx: Single mother of a 17-month-old; new partner introduced three months ago.

q: Every time he has a tantrum I’ve tried to redirect him and talk him through it.
cx: What she has tried.

q: I understand this kind of behaviour is normal for his age but I feel like I’m fighting a losing battle and I’m in a difficult position.
cx: Partner starting to dread visits.

q: We've been sneaking out to avoid the crying but I've read that actually makes it worse?
cx: One-year-old melts down when parents leave her with a new nanny.

q: Any tricks that actually worked for you? Feeling a bit guilty every time we leave 😅
cx: Grandparents leaving in a few days.

q: one time I was out with colleagues, while the kids, at home with the mom, ended up saying to her "why is Daddy out and not you?".
cx: Father who is the children's favourite parent.

q: She often says "I'm doing everything for them, I'm always available and sweet, you're more strict and not doing much for them and they still love you more than me... Why?"
cx: His wife's words about the preference.

q: So, here I am, being told she hates me, feeling guilty for being loved by my kids.
cx: The favourite parent's side.
